Question Choices: Select. In the ordered pair $(x, y)$, which number tells you how far to move left or right? ~~the-first-number | the-second-number~~
Solution: An ordered pair is (x,y): x gives horizontal position, followed by y for vertical position.

Question Choices: Fill: Point A is 4 units right of the origin and 3 units up. Write its coordinates. (__, __)
Hints: Right/up are positive; left/down are negative.
Solution: Horizontal motion gives x=4; vertical motion gives y=3. Write x first: (4,3).

Question Choices: Fill: Point B is 5 units left of the origin and 2 units down. Write its coordinates. (__, __)
Hints: Right/up are positive; left/down are negative.
Solution: Horizontal motion gives x=-5; vertical motion gives y=-2. Write x first: (-5,-2).

Question Choices: Select. In which quadrant is the point $(6, -3)$? ~~I | II | III | IV~~
Hints: Use both signs to choose one of the four quadrants.
Solution: The signs are x positive and y negative, placing the point in quadrant IV. Quadrants I, II, III, IV have signs (+,+), (−,+), (−,−), (+,−), respectively.

Question Choices: Select. In which quadrant is the point $(-7, -1)$? ~~I | II | III | IV~~
Hints: Use both signs to choose one of the four quadrants.
Solution: The signs are x negative and y negative, placing the point in quadrant III. Quadrants I, II, III, IV have signs (+,+), (−,+), (−,−), (+,−), respectively.

Question Choices: Select. Where is the point $(0, -4)$? ~~on-the-x-axis | on-the-y-axis | in-Quadrant-III | in-Quadrant-IV~~
Solution: At (0,-4), x=0, so there is no horizontal displacement and the point lies on the y-axis. An axis point belongs to no quadrant.

Question Choices: Fill: Point P is at $(3, 5)$. It is reflected over the x-axis. Write the coordinates of the new point. (__, __)
Hints: Keep the coordinate along the mirror axis; negate the other.
Solution: Reflecting across the x-axis keeps x and reverses y. Thus (3,5) becomes (3,-5); the perpendicular distance to the mirror axis is unchanged.

Question Choices: Fill: Point Q is at $(-2, 6)$. It is reflected over the y-axis. Write the coordinates of the new point. (__, __)
Hints: Keep the coordinate along the mirror axis; negate the other.
Solution: Reflecting across the y-axis keeps y and reverses x. Thus (-2,6) becomes (2,6); the perpendicular distance to the mirror axis is unchanged.
